title: Tech Note: Sending Sets
author: Jean-Yves Fock-Hoon
featured_technology: VARIABLE TO BLOB / BLOB TO VARIABLE serialization
EXECUTE ON CLIENT for broadcasting to registered 4D Clients
Interprocess Sets and CALL PROCESS-based UI refresh

historical_commentary.text: Jean-Yves Fock-Hoon (4D QA Manager) traces the evolution of sending a Set from one 4D Client to others across 4D 6.0.x, 6.5.x, and 6.7.x, showing how the new 6.7.x commands CREATE SET FROM ARRAY and BOOLEAN ARRAY FROM SET let a Set be converted directly to/from a Boolean array and shipped as a Blob via EXECUTE ON CLIENT, eliminating the older pattern of saving a Set to a temporary document that other clients had to reload. Sets and the classic client/server EXECUTE ON CLIENT/REGISTER CLIENT commands remain part of 4D today and this general document-free technique is still valid and usable, but most modern multi-client 4D architectures increasingly rely on ORDA/REST-based data access and newer synchronization patterns rather than manually broadcasting serialized Boolean arrays between classic 4D Clients, so the specific workaround is now a superseded (though still functional) technique for most new development.
related_updates: 4D's classic client/server architecture has been supplemented by ORDA and REST-based access, offering different patterns for sharing selections/state across clients
CREATE SET FROM ARRAY, BOOLEAN ARRAY FROM SET, and EXECUTE ON CLIENT remain part of the current 4D language, unchanged in core behavior since this note
4D Server has gained additional built-in interprocess/network communication commands since 2001 that reduce the need for this specific workaround
